articles.title: Suaalii keeps ‘open mindset’ to Wallabies position amid rising expectations for Rugby World Cup
articles.summary: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii won’t specialise in one on-field role yet. Australia coach Les Kiss faces multiple selection conundrums. He is known as the Wallabies’ foremost code-switcher, and there are growing calls for him to settle on a position that makes the most out of his unquestionable abilities.
body: Speaking at the NFL fan festival on Thursday to promote next year’s Rugby World Cup matches in Melbourne, Suaalii said he had no plans to specialise in just one on-field role.
“My personality and me as a human, I’ve always loved trying to master different positions,” he said.

“I feel like that’s the excitement with rugby. Myself, I know I can play 12, I know I can play 13, I know I can play fullback, I know I can play wing, hopefully when I’m a little bit older I can play 10 as well.
“I’m just having an open mindset to position, and just trying to be great at what I do.”

articles.title: ‘That’s how it started’: Dambrauskas’ journey from Who Wants to Be a Millionaire to Champions League
articles.summary: Valdas Dambrauskas takes Sabah to Manchester United after journeying from Lithuania and a game show win, via London pub work. Valdas Dambrauskas can reel off the questions and answers without a moment’s pause. Who won the first Academy Award for best actor in 1929?
body: It was enough to win Dambrauskas about £725 in his appearance on Six Zeros – A Million, the Lithuanian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? “At that time it was quite big money,” he says. “I could have bought a flat in my home town; it was a very difficult period there and they were almost free. But my plan was to go to England and follow my dream to become a coach, and that’s how it started.”

More than two and a half decades later the story continues at Old Trafford where Dambrauskas will manage the Azerbaijani champions, Sabah, in their Champions League debut on Thursday night. The club’s journey is some tale in itself given Sabah, who came through a dramatic playoff with Hapoel Be’er Sheva, did not exist until 2017. But the path taken by their head coach, a 25-year-old office worker with only a modest football background when his general knowledge skills were put on display, is virtually unparalleled in the modern game.

articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino believes Chelsea should be stripped of the Premier League title for 2016-17, when his Tottenham team finished runners-up.
body: Chelsea were fined £10.75m in March after being charged by the Premier League for historical breaches of competition rules.

articles.title: Chelsea’s 2016-17 Premier League title should be given to Spurs, says Pochettino
articles.summary: Former manager says Chelsea should be stripped of title. ‘The title should be for the team that was second’ Mauricio Pochettino says Chelsea should be stripped of their 2016-17 Premier League title for financial rule breaches and the honour retrospectively awarded to Tottenham, who he led to second…
body: Chelsea were fined £10m by the Football Association in July and given a suspended two-window transfer ban for multiple violations of the rules during the Roman Abramovich era. They were also fined £10.75m by the Premier League in March.

The club were found to have used unlicensed agents and sought to obscure the nature of their transfer business between 2009 and 2022. The deals that took Eden Hazard, Willian, David Luiz and Nemanja Matic to Stamford Bridge were among those found to have transgressed. Those players were central to Chelsea’s 2016-17 triumph under Antonio Conte.

The club’s BlueCo ownership self-reported the breaches when it took over from Abramovich in 2022 in the hope of mitigating the punishment, and the club avoided a points deduction. Pochettino, who went on to manage Chelsea in 2023-24 and is in charge of the US, believes the authorities did not go nearly far enough. His Spurs team finished seven points behind Conte’s Chelsea.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: ‘I am always open to help Tottenham. In whatever division’
articles.summary: Manager is excited by new US deal but might have returned to Spurs if the stars had aligned and does not rule out taking England job one day. If things had worked out differently, Mauricio Pochettino would have gone back to his beloved Tottenham over the summer.
body: Seriously, Mauricio? After a World Cup campaign with the United States and top jobs with Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain before that, he would have been willing to start a new chapter in the second tier of English football? “Yes, of course,” Pochettino says. “Tottenham … it’s the only club that always I am open to help. In whatever division.”

Football is about timing and Pochettino was left to reflect on how his stars did not align. It has been a theme of his managerial career, along with the desire to keep an eye out for greener pastures. And not be shy about doing so.

Spurs’ idea after sacking Thomas Frank in February was to get to the end of the season under the interim Igor Tudor, when they could assess a potentially deeper pool of candidates. They knew that if Pochettino was to be their man, they would have to wait for him because he was contracted to the US until after the World Cup. There was no way he could walk out on that challenge. Nor would he have wanted to.

articles.title: Barca's Rodri apologises over Valencia 'weak' comments
articles.summary: Barcelona midfielder Rodri says he has apologised to the entire Valencia squad after television cameras appeared to catch him describing the La Liga strugglers as "very weak".
body: Rodri reportedly made the comment to Barcelona team-mates Pau Cubarsi and Raphinha while sitting on the bench after being substituted during his side's 5-0 league win against Valencia on Sunday.
The result at Mestella Stadium left Valencia bottom of the table with no wins in their first four matches.
Though the footage has no audio, broadcaster Movistar claimed they lip-read the 30-year-old former Manchester City player saying: "They're really weak. They haven't got past the halfway line."
Fans and sections of the Spanish media accused Rodri, who won the golden ball as Spain won the 2026 World Cup, of being disrespectful.

articles.title: Why is there an NFL game in Australia?
articles.summary: The NFL has so far played regular-season games in seven international countries but this week's trip to Australia represents a new frontier for the USA's biggest sports league.
body: It is the NFL's first game in the Asia-Pacific region. The USA's biggest sports league is making its longest-ever road trip for the first of a record nine international games in 2026.
It will take place about 10,000 miles from the NFL's New York headquarters, in front of about 100,000 fans at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground.
That means the Los Angeles Rams will 'host' the San Francisco 49ers on a more open oval field on Friday (01:35 BST).
But when NFL commissioner Roger Goodell visited the MCG for the first time in April, he said the historic arena "speaks to you", and it says "this is the right place to be".

articles.title: Coco Gauff reveals why she hasn’t messaged Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe about US Open achievement
articles.summary: Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe are set to face off in a historic US Open semi-final. Coco Gauff was asked if she has reached out to them and the tennis star explained why she hasn’t. This has been a great US Open for American stars so far.
body: Shelton and Tiafoe will battle each other for a spot in the final, and it’s a clash that makes history. This is the first time two Black American men are battling in a Grand Slam semi-final in the Open era.
Naturally, there is a lot of excitement in the country about it. And Coco Gauff, as another Black tennis star, was asked about if she had reached out to them about this momentous occasion.
There is added significance to this piece of history, as it has been 58 years since the legendary Arthur Ashe won the US Open in 1968.
And when it was brought up to Gauff, she recognized that this is a huge moment, while also revealing her reason for not messaging either Shelton or Tiafoe about it.

articles.title: Zverev's US Open rocky road turns into smooth sailing to the semi-finals
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev ‌took another big step towards a second Grand Slam ‌title by beating Dutchman Botic van de ​Zandschulp 6-2 7-5 6-1 to reach the US Open semi-finals.
body: The 29-year-old French Open champion and Wimbledon runner-up got off to a slow start in his campaign at Flushing ​Meadows but has steadily found his range.
Zverev played five-set matches in each of the first two matches, but he has won his last three in straight sets and is the only man to reach all four Grand Slam semi-finals this year.
Into his 13th major semi-final, Zverev will face Karen Khachanov in the last four for a spot in Sunday's final.

"I ‌think you saw in the first two rounds, I really didn't play well," said Zverev, who has spent 16 hours and 40 minutes on court, the most by any man en route to the semi-finals at the US Open since 1991.

Then a few weeks later, another significant headline - Pochettino had, a little surprisingly perhaps, signed for four more years with the USA.
Where to start? I smile before jesting, and Pochettino just laughs and says he's ready. His reflections on the World Cup seem like as good a place to get going.
